title: Far memset/memcpy/memmove lengths above 65535 are truncated or deleted
summary: createFarMemLibcall truncated the length of an address-space-2 G_MEMSET, G_MEMCPY or G_MEMMOVE to 16 bits without a range check. A constant 70000-byte far memset called __memset_far with 4464, and a runtime i32 memcpy length lost its high 16 bits. The compiler exited 0 and the verifier was clean. The input's len64k function (a 65536-byte memmove from a near pointer, which the IRTranslator narrows to 16 bits and so deletes) is not a defect: LangRef "Allocated objects" bounds every allocated object by the largest signed integer of its index type, 32767 bytes for the 16-bit near space, so a near operand cannot be valid for 65536 bytes and len64k is undefined behaviour. Found by the independent review (finding B2) and reproduced on the downstream toolchain.

prior_work.source_assessment: Downstream MOSLegalizerInfo.cpp createFarMemLibcall builds buildTrunc(LLT::scalar(16), Len) for any wider length (0002 and 0013 carry the same hunk); the extracted patch 4 matches.
prior_work.binary_assessment: Downstream release llc 9031686c emits ldx #112 / ldy #17 (4464) for the 70000-byte fill and a bare rts for the 65536-byte memmove; the extracted candidate d7fde754 emits the same.
prior_work.decision: mos-far-memset-wrong-bank fixed near/far runtime routing and explicitly excluded lengths above 65535 from its closure. This is the length-domain defect in the same function, a separate mechanism.

configuration.expected: lengths above 0xFFFF are rejected, split or passed to a 32-bit-length entry

resolution.change: patches/llvm-mos/0002-321-accum16.patch: createFarMemLibcall (MOSLegalizerInfo.cpp) keeps the 16-bit __memset_far/__memcpy_far/__memmove_far call only when the length is at most 16 bits, a constant <= 0xFFFF, or has known bits (LegalizerHelper::getValueTracking()) clearing bits 16 and up; any other length calls __memset_far32/__memcpy_far32/__memmove_far32 with a uint32_t length. platforms/snes/mem-far.c adds those three entries as weak C functions with the same direction rule for memmove.
resolution.causal_explanation: createFarMemLibcall built G_TRUNC to s16 of every wider length without a range check, so 70000 became 4464 and a runtime i32 length lost its high half. Lengths that are not provably 16-bit now keep all 32 bits and reach a runtime entry that loops over a uint32_t index, so no length is truncated; provable lengths keep the identical 16-bit call.
resolution.trigger_check: The unchanged farmemlen.ll runs through the candidate llc with the baseline configuration; the runner passes only when big_const tail-calls __memset_far32 and big_var tail-calls __memcpy_far32. len64k is excluded because it is undefined behaviour (see summary).
regression_tests: llvm/test/CodeGen/MOS/far-memop-length.ll (in 0002): 65535 stays 16-bit; 65536, 65537, 70000, unbounded i32 and zext(n)*2 use the 32-bit entries; zext i16, and-0xFFFF and i16 lengths stay 16-bit

dev/far_memops32.sh with examples/65816/far_memops32.c: 70000-byte fills, a 69984-byte overlapping move and a 32 KiB copy across $7E/$7F, +mos-a16 and +mos-a16,+mos-xy16 at -Os and -O2, corpus_result == 0xFFFF on MAME and bsnes-jg

" "$out" | grep -A8 "^big_const:" | grep -q -E "(jmp|jsr)[[:space:]]+__memset_far32$"; then echo "FAIL: 70000-byte far memset does not call __memset_far32"; bad=1; fi; if ! printf "%s
" "$out" | grep -A2 "^big_var:" | grep -q -E "(jmp|jsr)[[:space:]]+__memcpy_far32$"; then echo "FAIL: unbounded i32 far memcpy does not call __memcpy_far32"; bad=1; fi; echo "NOTE: len64k is not checked: a 65536-byte memmove from a near (addrspace 0) source is undefined behaviour, because LangRef (Allocated objects) bounds a near object by 32767 bytes; its deletion after the IRTranslator narrows the length to 16 bits is sound."; [ $bad = 0 ] && echo "PASS: lengths above 0xFFFF reach the 32-bit-length far runtime"; exit $bad
